self_flagged_distractors.why_possibly_correct: Historically true: state legislatures chose U.S. senators before the 17th Amendment (1913). The stem is present tense, so 'citizens from their state' is the only current answer, but a historical reading could defend it.
The Senate's advice-and-consent role is a real part of the appointment process; a pedantic reading of 'appoints' could partially defend it. Official bank answer is the President.
Paying federal taxes is a real civic duty and could be defended as 'civic participation' in ordinary speech; the bank's own taxonomy assigns it to Q70/Q71, not Q69.
Joining a political party could be defended as a way of serving the country in ordinary speech; the bank's taxonomy assigns it to civic participation (Q69), not Q70.
Native Americans were also historically enslaved in colonial America; the official bank answer is Africans, but a historically-informed reading could partially defend this option.

The bank also accepts the unqualified 'Freed the slaves' for Q95, so the line between this distractor and an acceptable loose answer is thin; the distractor is wrong precisely because the Proclamation did NOT reach everywhere — the 13th Amendment did.
Hoover WAS president during the Depression's first years (1929–33); the stem's 'and World War II' makes FDR the only correct answer, but a partial reading could defend Hoover.

German U-boats did attack U.S. ships in the Atlantic before the December 1941 declaration of war; the official bank cause for WWII entry is Pearl Harbor/Allies/Axis, but a well-read candidate could partially defend this option.
